newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler in no hurry on management changes.
newsitem.headline: Daimler in no hurry on management changes.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG said on Wednesday it was under no time pressure to make management changes despite speculation that the biggest German industrial group was planning to make an announcement this week.
Daimler spokesman Roland Klein said it was not conceivable that a decision would be announced following a regular management board meeting on Wednesday.
"There exists no pressure to make a decision," he said, adding that it was well known that such changes were under discussion by Daimler chairman Juergen Schrempp.
Klein played down media reports that a power play was taking place at the top of Daimler and that management changes under discussion were linked to making the group more efficient.

German media reports have focused on the supposed opposition of Helmut Werner, chairman of Daimler's Mercedes car subsidiary, to plans to concentrate more power in the hands of the central Daimler group management.
A number of reports repeated a suggestion, previously denied by Daimler, that Werner would be offered a top position within the new Daimler board.

Schrempp said in late September that he hoped to make a decision on management restructuring by the end of the year. He said the measures would consider how to make decision-making faster and improve quality.
